node_kinds.name: GhostHound_TombstoneUser
node_kinds.description: A deleted AD user object, enumerated from CN=Deleted Objects via the SHOW_DELETED LDAP control. Properties record its AD Recycle Bin state (is_recycled) and whether it can be restored with its former group memberships intact (group_membership_recoverable, per the Deleted-vs-Recycled distinction in docs/adr/0004).

node_kinds.name: GhostHound_TombstoneComputer
node_kinds.description: A deleted AD computer object, enumerated from CN=Deleted Objects via the SHOW_DELETED LDAP control.

node_kinds.name: GhostHound_TombstoneGroup
node_kinds.description: A deleted AD group object, enumerated from CN=Deleted Objects via the SHOW_DELETED LDAP control.

relationship_kinds.name: GhostHound_CanReanimate
relationship_kinds.description: The source principal can restore the target tombstone via LDAP_SERVER_SHOW_DELETED_OID, by either of two mechanisms, recorded on the edge's `source` property (single strongest mechanism) and `sources` property (all of them). `reanimate_right`: the principal already holds the Reanimate-Tombstones control access right (or an unscoped control-access grant, which implies it), read off the domain naming context root. `owner`/`write_dac`/`write_owner`: the principal owns the tombstone, or holds WRITE_DAC/WRITE_OWNER on its own nTSecurityDescriptor, and can therefore rewrite that DACL to grant itself the right first -- an extra, auditable step, so filter on `source` when that distinction matters. See docs/adr/0001, docs/adr/0004 and docs/adr/0007.

relationship_kinds.name: GhostHound_WasMemberOf
relationship_kinds.description: The tombstone was a member of the target group at deletion time, and that membership is still preserved (group_membership_recoverable=true on the source node) because the object hasn't yet reached the fully-stripped AD Recycle Bin 'Recycled' state. Restoring the tombstone restores this membership too.

relationship_kinds.name: GhostHound_SameAs
relationship_kinds.description: Links a GhostHound-sourced placeholder node for a real AD principal (e.g. Domain Admins, referenced by CanReanimate/WasMemberOf) to the actual node RustHound-CE/SharpHound already created for it. BloodHound's OpenGraph ingest cannot merge these directly (docs/adr/0006), so this edge is created separately by running bridge_shadow_nodes.cypher against Neo4j after each import.
